t: For construction, acquisition, expansion, rehabilitation, and conversion of facilities for the training and administration of the reserve components of the Navy and Marine Corps as authorized by chapter 133 of title 10, United States Code, as amended, and the Reserve Forces Facilities Acts, $18,300,000, to remain available until September 30, 1984.

fable.w: This is a plain appropriation of funds for Navy and Marine Corps reserve facilities. There is no tempting participation reading: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any decision.
fable.s: For construction, acquisition, expansion, rehabilitation, and conversion of facilities for the training and administration of the reserve components of the Navy and Marine Corps

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations provision that authorizes a specific amount of funding for military facility construction and maintenance. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The text refers only to internal government actions (construction, acquisition) and legal authorizations.
qwen_block.s: For construction, acquisition, expansion, rehabilitation, and conversion of facilities for the training and administration of the reserve components of the Navy and Marine Corps as authorized by chapter 133 of title 10, United States Code, as amended, and the Reserve Forces Facilities Acts, $18,300,000, to remain available until September 30, 1984.

opus.w: This is a plain appropriation of $18,300,000 for building and converting Navy and Marine Corps reserve facilities. It does not require consultation, a hearing, a comment period, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue. References to the authorizing statutes don't create any process that brings outside parties into a federal decision.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions "reserve components" and refers to authorizing statutes, so it might seem to involve outside parties or rulemaking. It doesn't. It is only an appropriation for military reserve facilities. No one outside the federal government is consulted, there is no hearing or comment period, and it grants no right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard appropriation clause authorizing funds for military facility construction. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The only actors mentioned are federal military branches and the statutory authorization itself.
qwen_chat.s: For construction, acquisition, expansion, rehabilitation, and conversion of facilities for the training and administration of the reserve components of the Navy and Marine Corps as authorized by chapter 133 of title 10, United States Code, as amended, and the Reserve Forces Facilities Acts, $18,300,000, to remain available until September 30, 1984.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "reserve components" involve civilians or that the construction affects the public, implying some form of participation. However, the text is purely an appropriation clause authorizing funds for specific military purposes. It does not mandate any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory process involving non-federal entities. The actors involved (Navy, Marine Corps, Congress via appropriation) are all inside the federal government.
